# wallix-bastion_externalauth_oidc (Resource)

Provides an OIDC external authentication resource. It requires API v3.12 or later, and Terraform
1.11 or later for its write-only client secret.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "wallix-bastion_externalauth_oidc" "corporate" {
  authentication_name      = "corporate_oidc"
  timeout                  = 30
  client_id                = "bastion"
  client_secret_wo         = var.oidc_client_secret
  client_secret_wo_version = 1
  discovery_url            = "https://idp.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration"

  claim_customization {
    username    = "preferred_username"
    group       = "groups"
    email       = "email"
    displayname = "name"
  }
}
```

### With the OpenID Provider Metadata

```terraform
data "http" "oidc_discovery" {
  url = "https://idp.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration"
}

locals {
  oidc = jsondecode(data.http.oidc_discovery.response_body)
}

resource "wallix-bastion_externalauth_oidc" "corporate" {
  authentication_name      = "corporate_oidc"
  timeout                  = 30
  client_id                = "bastion"
  client_secret_wo         = var.oidc_client_secret
  client_secret_wo_version = 1
  discovery_url            = "https://idp.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration"

  claim_customization {
    username = "preferred_username"
    group    = "groups"
  }

  oidc_advanced_attributes {
    issuer                                = local.oidc.issuer
    scope                                 = ["openid", "profile", "email"]
    authorization_endpoint                = local.oidc.authorization_endpoint
    token_endpoint                        = local.oidc.token_endpoint
    userinfo_url_endpoint                 = local.oidc.userinfo_endpoint
    jwks_uri                              = local.oidc.jwks_uri
    id_token_signing_alg_values_supported = local.oidc.id_token_signing_alg_values_supported
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `authentication_name` (String)
- `client_id` (String)
- `timeout` (Number) Timeout of the requests to the identity provider, in seconds (1 to 900).

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `claim_customization` (Block, Optional) Names of the OIDC claims that hold the user attributes. Required. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--claim_customization))
- `client_secret_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Client secret, write-only (Terraform 1.11 and later): sent to the Bastion, never stored in the state. Change client_secret_wo_version to send a new value.
- `client_secret_wo_version` (Number) Version of client_secret_wo: a change sends the secret again. Removing both removes the secret from the Bastion.
- `description` (String)
- `discovery_url` (String) URL of the OpenID Provider metadata (.well-known/openid-configuration).
- `oidc_advanced_attributes` (Block, Optional) OpenID Provider metadata, as published at discovery_url. The Bastion cannot remove it: removing the block replaces the external authentication. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--oidc_advanced_attributes))
- `redirect_uri` (String) Redirection URI of the Bastion, its /api/oidc URL when not set. The Bastion does not update it: a change replaces the external authentication.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) ID of the external authentication on the Bastion.

<a id="nestedblock--claim_customization"></a>

### Nested Schema for `claim_customization`

Required:

- `username` (String) Claim of the user name.

Optional:

- `displayname` (String) Claim of the display name.
- `email` (String) Claim of the email.
- `group` (String) Claim of the user groups.
- `language` (String) Claim of the language.

<a id="nestedblock--oidc_advanced_attributes"></a>

### Nested Schema for `oidc_advanced_attributes`

Optional:

- `authorization_endpoint` (String) Authorization endpoint. Required with the block.
- `grant_type` (String) authorization_code, the only grant type of the Bastion.
- `id_token_signing_alg_values_supported` (List of String) JWS signing algorithms of the ID token. Required with the block.
- `issuer` (String) Issuer identifier of the OpenID Provider. Required with the block.
- `jwks_uri` (String) URL of the JSON Web Key Set. Required with the block.
- `response_type` (String) code, the only response type of the Bastion.
- `scope` (List of String) Scopes requested. Required with the block.
- `token_endpoint` (String) Token endpoint. Required with the block.
- `userinfo_url_endpoint` (String) UserInfo endpoint.

## Usage Notes

### Client Secret

`client_secret_wo` is a write-only argument: Terraform sends it to the Bastion and never stores it
in the state or the plan. Terraform cannot compare it with a previous value either, so a new secret
is only sent when `client_secret_wo_version` changes (or with any other change of the resource).
To rotate the secret, change both:

```terraform
  client_secret_wo         = var.oidc_client_secret
  client_secret_wo_version = 2
```

The Bastion never returns the secret, only whether one is set. With `client_secret_wo_version`
set, a secret removed outside Terraform shows in the next plan as the version added back, and the
apply sends it again; without a version, Terraform does not notice. Removing both arguments from
the configuration removes the secret from the Bastion. `client_secret_wo_version` cannot be set
without `client_secret_wo`.

Write-only arguments need Terraform 1.11 or later. An older Terraform rejects the configuration
before any change.

### Claims

`claim_customization` names the claims of the ID token that hold the user attributes. The Bastion
requires `username`, and `group` when users get their groups from the identity provider.

### OpenID Provider Metadata

The Bastion does not read `discovery_url` when the external authentication is created. The
endpoints and keys of the OpenID Provider go in `oidc_advanced_attributes`, for example from the
discovery document as above. When the block is set, the Bastion requires every argument but
`userinfo_url_endpoint`; `grant_type` and `response_type` default to the only values it supports.
The Bastion cannot remove these values: removing the block replaces the external authentication.

### redirect_uri

The Bastion computes `redirect_uri` (`https://<bastion>/api/oidc`) when it is not set; register
it as a redirection URI of the client on the identity provider. It can only be set at creation:
changing it replaces the external authentication.

### Deletion and Replacement

The Bastion refuses to delete an external authentication still used by an authentication domain.
A `wallix-bastion_authdomain_oidc` that references `authentication_name` is destroyed first.

The same refusal stops a replacement (change of `redirect_uri`, removal of
`oidc_advanced_attributes`) while a domain uses the external authentication: the apply fails with
a 409 before anything is deleted, and `create_before_destroy` cannot help since the name must be
unique. Remove it from the `external_auths` of its domains and apply, then make the change and add
it back.

## Import

OIDC external authentication can be imported using its `authentication_name`, e.g.

```shell
terraform import wallix-bastion_externalauth_oidc.corporate corporate_oidc
```

The import cannot read the secret: after it, the next apply sends `client_secret_wo` with
`client_secret_wo_version`.
